passages.title: Stars, Rain and a Goat
passages.passage: Every summer my cousins and I spend one night at a camp in the hills behind my grandmother's village. This year the weather forecast (1)____ rain, but we decided to go anyway. We (2)____ up our tent before the sun went down, which turned out to be a wise choice, because the first drops fell while we were still collecting firewood. My uncle, (3)____ has camped there since he was a boy, showed us how to keep the fire burning (4)____ spite of the wet wood. By nine o'clock the rain had stopped and the sky was full of stars. My little cousin Bao, who is only seven, had never seen (5)____ a clear sky in his life and kept asking whether the stars were real. We sat close to the fire and told stories until we could hardly (6)____ our eyes open. Sleeping on the ground is not comfortable, and I woke up several times during the night. At one point I heard a strange noise outside the tent and was (7)____ frightened that I could not move. In the morning we discovered that the noise had been made by a goat (8)____ to my grandmother's neighbour. Everyone laughed at me, but I did not (9)____ it seriously. Before we left, we made sure the fire was completely out and picked up every piece of rubbish. If we (10)____ the place dirty, my uncle would never take us again.

questions.q: Blank (1): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: A forecast predicts rain: the verb takes the weather directly as its object. Warned needs of/about, and told and informed need a person as their object.

questions.q: Blank (2): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The phrasal verb for building a tent is put up. Take up means start a hobby, and make up and get up have nothing to do with tents.

questions.q: Blank (3): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun is the subject of has camped and refers to a person, so it must be who. Whom is only for objects, which is for things, and whose shows possession.

questions.q: Blank (4): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase is in spite of, meaning despite. No other preposition can replace in here.

questions.q: Blank (5): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Before a + adjective + noun we use such: such a clear sky. So, too and very go directly in front of an adjective, not in front of a.

questions.q: Blank (6): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: You keep your eyes open: keep takes an object and an adjective. Stay, remain and last cannot take our eyes as an object.

questions.q: Blank (7): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The pattern is so + adjective + that clause: so frightened that I could not move. Such needs a noun, and too and very are not followed by a that clause of result.

questions.q: Blank (8): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: A reduced relative clause uses the -ing participle: a goat belonging to my grandmother's neighbour = a goat which belonged to her. The finite forms would need which or that before them.

questions.q: Blank (9): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The collocation is take something seriously. Get, make and have do not combine with seriously in this way.

questions.q: Blank (10): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The main clause has would never take, so this is a second conditional and the if clause needs the past simple left. Present forms would belong to a first conditional with will.

passages.title: Five Books at a Time
passages.passage: Until last month I had never been inside the public library in our district. My English teacher kept telling us that the library had (1)____ of graded readers, so one Saturday I finally went to have a look. To borrow anything you need a card, and getting one is not (2)____ difficult as I had expected. I (3)____ in a short form with my name, address and school, and a librarian checked my student card. She explained that members (4)____ borrow up to five books at a time and keep them for three weeks. If a book is returned late, you (5)____ pay a small fine for each day. I chose two novels and a book about space, (6)____ I had wanted to read since I saw a film about the planets. The librarian told me that the reading room on the second floor is (7)____ quietest place in the building, and she was right. I sat there for two hours (8)____ anybody disturbing me. Since then I have been going back every weekend. Sometimes I meet my friend Hoa there, and we test each other (9)____ new words from the books we have read. My mother says it is the best thing I have done all year, and I think she may (10)____ right. The card cost nothing, but it has already given me a new habit.

questions.q: Blank (1): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Plenty of works before any noun and means a large number. Much of, many of and several of need the or a pronoun after them (many of the readers).

questions.q: Blank (2): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The comparison of equality is as + adjective + as, and after not the first as still fits. That, such and too cannot be followed by the second as.

questions.q: Blank (3): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: You fill in a form. Completed would need no in, and wrote in and put in do not describe filling a form.

questions.q: Blank (4): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The sentence describes what members are allowed to do, so the modal is can. Must and should would make borrowing five books an obligation, and need is not followed by a bare verb in an affirmative sentence.

questions.q: Blank (5): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: A rule that cannot be avoided uses must + bare verb. Have and ought would need to pay, and need pay is not used in an affirmative sentence.

questions.q: Blank (6): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: After a comma, a non-defining relative clause about a thing takes which. That is not used after a comma, what is not a relative pronoun here, and whom is for people.

questions.q: Blank (7): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: A superlative such as quietest is normally preceded by the. A, an and every do not go with a superlative that picks out one place.

questions.q: Blank (8): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The meaning is that nobody disturbed the writer, which is expressed by without + -ing. With anybody disturbing me means the opposite, and except and besides do not fit the -ing phrase.

questions.q: Blank (9): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: You test somebody on the material they have learned. In, for and about do not follow test in this meaning.

questions.q: Blank (10): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: After a modal verb such as may we need the bare infinitive be. Is, been and being cannot follow a modal directly.

passages.title: Desks in a Circle
passages.passage: I always feel nervous on the first day of term, even though I have been going to the same school (1)____ six years. This September was different, because our class had been moved to a new building on the other side of the playground. I arrived early, (2)____ I could find my classroom without asking anyone. The corridor was so long that I walked past the door twice (3)____ I noticed the number. Inside, the desks were arranged in a circle rather than in rows, (4)____ meant we could all see each other. Our new form teacher, Mr Tuan, greeted us at the door and asked us to (5)____ ourselves up in alphabetical order. That took a surprisingly long time, as nobody could remember (6)____ to spell the other students' surnames. After that he handed out the timetable and explained the rules. We are not (7)____ to use our phones in class, but we may bring them to school for emergencies. At break my old friends and I went to look at the new library, which is twice (8)____ size of the old one. By the end of the day I had stopped worrying. Nothing had gone wrong, and I had even made a new friend (9)____ sits next to me in maths. Perhaps next year I will not feel nervous (10)____ all.

questions.q: Blank (1): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: With the present perfect continuous, a length of time (six years) takes for. Since needs a starting point such as 2020, and during and in do not measure how long an action has continued.

questions.q: Blank (2): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Arriving early was done in order to find the room, so the linker of purpose is so (that). Because would give the reason, and although and unless make no sense here.

questions.q: Blank (3): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The writer walked past the door and only then noticed the number, so the two actions are joined by before. After reverses the order, and while and since do not fit the sequence.

questions.q: Blank (4): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: A relative clause that comments on the whole previous idea, after a comma, uses which. That cannot follow a comma this way, what is not a relative pronoun, and who refers to people.

questions.q: Blank (5): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The phrasal verb is line up: to form a line. Set up means organise or prepare, and stand and put do not combine with ourselves up to describe forming a line.

questions.q: Blank (6): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The question word before to spell must be how, because spelling is a way of doing something. What, which and where would need a different structure or make no sense.

questions.q: Blank (7): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Permission in the passive is be allowed to. Let is not used in the passive with to, and made and forced would mean somebody obliged the students to use phones.

questions.q: Blank (8): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The comparison is twice the size of. A, its and that do not form this fixed pattern with twice.

questions.q: Blank (9): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The pronoun is the subject of sits and refers to a person, so it must be who. Whom is an object form, which is for things, and whose shows possession.

questions.q: Blank (10): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase not ... at all adds emphasis to a negative. No other preposition combines with all in this meaning.

passages.title: Two Days Without a Screen
passages.passage: Last Tuesday my phone fell (1)____ of my pocket on the stairs at school, and the screen broke into a hundred tiny pieces. It still switched on, but I could hardly read anything. My first thought was that my parents would be angry, (2)____ the phone was a birthday present from them only three months before. I decided to tell them straight away rather (3)____ hide it, and I am glad I did. My father looked at the screen, sighed, and said that accidents happen to everyone. The next day we (4)____ it to a small repair shop near the market. The man there told us that a new screen would cost about a third of the price of the phone and that it would be ready (5)____ two days. While I was waiting, I discovered how much I depend (6)____ my phone. I could not check the time, message my friends or look (7)____ words in my dictionary app. On the other hand, I finished my homework faster than usual and went to bed earlier. When I picked the phone up on Thursday, it looked (8)____ if nothing had ever happened to it. My father made me buy a proper case (9)____ that it would not happen again. I have learned a lesson (10)____ I hope I will not need to learn twice.

questions.q: Blank (1): type one word.
questions.explanation: Something falls out of a pocket; the two-part preposition out of shows movement from inside. Off or from cannot be followed by of here.

questions.q: Blank (2): type one word.
questions.explanation: The second clause gives the reason the parents might be angry, so a reason linker such as because (or as, since) fits. So would reverse cause and result, and but would make the two ideas contrast, which they do not.

questions.q: Blank (3): type one word.
questions.explanation: The fixed pattern is rather than + bare verb: tell them rather than hide it. Then is a common misspelling, and instead would need of hiding.

questions.q: Blank (4): type one word.
questions.explanation: You take something to a shop, and the narrative is in the past simple, so took. Went fails because it cannot have it as an object, and the present form take breaks the past narrative.

questions.q: Blank (5): type one word.
questions.explanation: A future point measured from now is expressed with in two days (or within). For two days would describe a duration, not the moment the phone is ready.

questions.q: Blank (6): type one word.
questions.explanation: The verb takes a fixed preposition: depend on (or the more formal upon). Of is a common mistake, influenced by independent of, but depend of is not English.

questions.q: Blank (7): type one word.
questions.explanation: To search for a word in a dictionary is to look it up. Look for means to try to find something lost, and look at only means to direct your eyes.

questions.q: Blank (8): type one word.
questions.explanation: The comparison with an imagined situation is as if + past perfect. Like if is not standard English, and even if would change the meaning.

questions.q: Blank (9): type one word.
questions.explanation: Purpose is expressed by so that + clause: he made me buy a case so that it would not happen again. In order that is two words, and because that is not English.

questions.q: Blank (10): type one word.
questions.explanation: A defining relative clause about a thing (a lesson) with no comma takes which or that. What cannot follow a noun as a relative pronoun, and who is for people.
